guidance: A field measurement of fuel input, not a safety or efficiency check. Clock the meter only with every other gas appliance and standing pilot off, at steady state and at the stage being tested, and follow the appliance manufacturer's instructions. The heating value must come from the gas supplier or the bill; the default is a national average. An out-of-band result calls for manifold pressure, orifice and altitude checks by a qualified technician.
method: Input rate is derived from the volume a gas meter test dial passes in a measured time. ft3/h = dial size in ft3 per revolution x revolutions timed x 3600 / seconds, so a 1/2 ft3 dial turning once in 20 s gives 90 ft3/h. The measured input is ft3/h x the fuel heating value in BTU/ft3 (default 1030, the approximate US average; propane is about 2500; a utility's own figure is better), with power in kW at 3412.14 BTU/kWh and therms at 100,000 BTU. With a nameplate input the page reports percent of nameplate, the signed deviation, and the time one dial revolution should take at that rating; it marks the result on rate inside +/-5%, outside that but inside +/-10%, and well outside. The +/-5% band and clocking the meter as an accepted procedure come from ANSI/ACCA 5 QI section 4.5. The 1/time relation also gives the sensitivity, the measured input divided by the seconds timed per second of timing error. Numbers accept a decimal comma or point and thousands separators; exponent notation and signs are refused, as are times from 0.5 to 3600 s outside range, fractional or 1-20 revolutions outside range, heating values outside 500-3000 BTU/ft3, nameplate inputs outside 1,000-2,000,000 BTU/h and flows above 10,000 ft3/h. Only imperial test dials are supported: metric meters are read on the drum and digital meters without a test dial cannot be clocked. The page does not measure manifold pressure, temperature rise, CO or steady-state efficiency and makes no safety determination.
